derived_by: read out of the cached HTML by a human; NOT captured from the extractor
note: This is the ADVERSE case in the set and it is here on purpose. The page's single Book scope repeats itemprop="name" three times (a mobile copy of the work title, a desktop copy, and the 'Book Details' section heading), so the record has no single name. It also describes a Turkish EDITION of a work the URL calls 'The Lord of the Rings'. The expectations below pin what the extractor actually does with that, so that a future change to the naming rule fails here and is read by a person.
separator_ambiguity: The two multi-valued expectations below ('name' and 'isbn') are hand-read as the JOINED value, and they can only be checked because the checker reconstructs them. `structured._line` joins FIELDS with '; ' and `_collect` joins the members of a multi-valued property with '; ' too, so once the line is rendered 'isbn: 9753423470; 9789753423472' is indistinguishable from an isbn followed by a loose number -- to this checker, to a reader, and to the model. The checker's rule (a chunk with no 'key: ' prefix continues the previous value) is a GUESS, is flagged as separator_ambiguous in the report, and is recorded here rather than hidden inside a passing assertion.
quoted_source:
Yüzüklerin Efendisi

(appears twice: mobile + desktop)
<span itemprop="aggregateRating" itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/AggregateRating"> <meta itemprop="ratingValue" content="4.45"/> <meta itemprop="ratingCount" content="118"/> ...

expectations.read_from: content="4.45" on the AggregateRating meta. THE FINDING: the rating lands on a record whose head is the bare type 'Book' -- there is no entity name -- because itemprop="name" occurs three times, becomes a list, and the name lookup only accepts a scalar. entity_is_bare_type is asserted TRUE deliberately: it is the defect, pinned. No bestRating is stated, so the value correctly carries no '/5'.
content="118"; kept beside ratingValue so the count is not read as a second score

expectations.value: Yüzüklerin Efendisi; Yüzüklerin Efendisi; Book Details
expectations.read_from: the three itemprop="name" elements, in document order, joined by the list separator. Asserted exactly as it renders -- including the duplicate and the section heading -- because that string is what a reader and the model actually see.
the ISBN-10 and ISBN-13 cells; a repeated property that SHOULD be a list, and here is one
2007; the Turkish edition's year, not the 1954 first-publication year the page also displays

known_absent.reason: <a itemprop="author"> yields its href, so the value is '/authors/OL26320A/J.R.R._Tolkien; /authors/OL26320A/J.R.R._Tolkien' -- a path, twice. The author's name as written is not recovered. Same root cause as the Gutenberg creator field.
<a itemprop="publisher"> yields '/publishers/Metis_Yayıncılık'. The readable publisher name is in the link text and is discarded.

The title the URL and the page heading use is NOT inside the Book scope as an itemprop, so no record names it. A query about The Lord of the Rings that retrieves this line gets a 4.45 attached to a Turkish edition title and a bare type.
